title: Cross-Cloud Identity Federation Monitoring

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.22 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.22 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudtrail` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (  eventName="AssumeRoleWithSAML")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.22_cross_cloud_identity_fed_22"
| sort -_time
description: Federation misconfiguration or token abuse spans IdPs and cloud consoles; unified visibility reduces blind spots for lateral movement across AWS, Azure, and GCP.
value: Detecting cross-cloud identity federation monitoring early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Normalize federated principal fields into a common `user` or `subject` via `eval`/`lookup`. Ingest IdP logs (Okta, Entra ID) via HEC if available and join on session ID. Alert on unusual federation volume, new IdP thumbprint, or cross-cloud sessions within minutes for the same user.
visualization: Table (cloud, user, count), Timeline (federation events), Sankey or chord (IdP to cloud role).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` count
  from datamodel=Change.All_Changes
  by All_Changes.user All_Changes.object_category All_Changes.action span=1h
| sort -count
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Normalize federated principal fields into a common `user` or `subject` via `eval`/`lookup`. Ingest IdP logs (Okta, Entra ID) via HEC if available and join on session ID. Alert on unusual federation volume, new IdP thumbprint, or cross-cloud sessions within minutes for the same user.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" (  eventName="AssumeRoleWithSAML")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.22_cross_cloud_identity_fed_22"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect cross-cloud identity federation monitoring. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_22_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Table (cloud, user, count), Timeline (federation events), Sankey or chord (IdP to cloud role)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`, `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cross-cloud identity federation monitoring so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
